qc:current-surface.jarvis_gap: The current surface is a well-engineered, honest transport layer (accurate SSE/Stop receipts, no fabricated confirmations, shared error classification) but it is not yet a JARVIS voice: it renders assistant replies as near-plain-text (no bold/lists/links/tables), gives visibility into tool calls only as raw collapsed JSON with no per-tool semantics, and — most importantly for 'see what I'm looking at' — page-context enrichment beyond the bare route/query string exists on exactly one of ~60 routes (EntityDetailPage) and is entirely absent from the butler-detail ChatPanel Sheet, so today the butler mostly does not know what the owner is looking at outside one page, and never when chatting from a butler's own detail Sheet. On top of that, ChatPanel.tsx and FloatingChatWidget.tsx are ~250-line near-duplicates of the same send/stream/stop state machine that have already drifted (page_context is wired into one and silently missing from the other), which is both a correctness risk today and a tax on every future change to this spine.

findings.title: ChatPanel.tsx never sends page_context — only FloatingChatWidget does
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/chat/ChatPanel.tsx:364-376 calls createConversation/sendMessage with a bare `{ message: trimmed, message_id: messageId }` body and never imports usePageContextCapture; contrast frontend/src/components/chat/FloatingChatWidget.tsx:112-118,338,344,350 which builds `buildMessagePayload(trimmed, messageId, pageContext)` from `usePageContextCapture()`.
findings.detail: The butler-detail Sheet (opened from any butler's own page via ChatPanel) is a fully separate chat surface from the floating widget, sharing the same conversation store, but it can never ground a reply in 'what the owner is looking at' — even on the one page (EntityDetailPage) that does enrich page context, opening chat via ChatPanel instead of the floating widget silently drops that enrichment. This is exactly the kind of surface owners will use when already on a butler's detail page wanting to ask about it, and it is the one place page-context grounding is guaranteed to matter most.

findings.title: Page-context enrichment (entity_ref) is wired into exactly 1 of ~60 routes
findings.evidence: frontend/src/pages/EntityDetailPage.tsx:2378 is the only call site of `usePageContext().set(...)` outside page-context.tsx itself (grep across frontend/src/pages and frontend/src/router-config.tsx, which lists 60 `path:` entries, found no other callers).
findings.detail: Every other page (butler dashboards, ingestion, sessions, approvals, memory views, etc.) contributes only the auto-captured `{route, query_params}` — no `entity_ref`, and nothing richer (no summarized page state, visible table rows, or the specific record on screen). For the north-star promise ('converse about WHAT THEY ARE LOOKING AT' from any page), today that promise is honored only in one place; everywhere else the routed butler gets a bare path string and must independently re-derive context via tool calls, if it can at all.

findings.title: Assistant markdown rendering is code-fence-only — no bold/italic/lists/headers/links/tables

frontend/src/components/chat/MessageThread.tsx:46-75 (`SimpleMarkdown`) splits only on ``` fenced blocks; every non-fence segment is rendered as a literal `

` with no further parsing.

lens:page-context.jarvis_gap: Today the chat does not know what the owner is looking at; it knows only where the browser bar points. The entire contract is `{route, query_params, entity_ref}` (src/butlers/api/models/conversation.py:16-30), the enrichment type physically cannot express anything beyond an entity string (frontend/src/lib/page-context.tsx:45-47), and exactly one of the 46 shell destinations enriches it (frontend/src/pages/EntityDetailPage.tsx:2378-2382). It is captured at send time with no timestamp, never persisted (frontend/src/components/chat/FloatingChatWidget.tsx:338; src/butlers/api/routers/conversations.py:815-841), shown to nobody, removable by nobody, and injected as one unfenced JSON line into two prompts (src/butlers/modules/pipeline.py:593-597; src/butlers/core_tools/_switchboard.py:88-89) that the answering butler has no tool to verify — it cannot re-read the cross-schema data the page rendered, because butler DB roles are schema-scoped while only the API's DatabaseManager fans out across schemas. Worse, the one deterministic injector lives inside `route_to_butler`, so the moment a conversation becomes sticky-routed (`pinned_target = routed_butler`, src/butlers/api/routers/conversations.py:1601-1612) the classification hop is bypassed and the policy-bypass envelope carries prompt only (src/butlers/modules/pipeline.py:2419-2421) — every follow-up message in a mature conversation arrives context-blind. For the north star's question lane ("why is this trending up?" asked from /health/measurements) the butler receives literally `{"route": "/health/measurements"}` while the chart's window and its degraded banners live in component state (frontend/src/components/health/MeasurementChart.tsx:118-123, 259, 337, 427). The distance is a whole architecture: a typed ViewRef the shell derives from its own capability manifest, a server-side snapshot resolved by re-querying the same read models the page rendered from, a fenced structured block that reaches the butler on every path, a refresh tool, durable persistence, and a visible removable chip so the owner knows what they attached.

findings.title: The page-context contract is three fields and structurally cannot grow
findings.evidence: frontend/src/lib/page-context.tsx:45-47; src/butlers/api/models/conversation.py:16-30; frontend/src/api/types.ts:5483-5487
findings.detail: `PageContextEnrichment` declares exactly one optional field (`entity_ref?: string | null`), and the API model is `{route, query_params, entity_ref}`. There is no way for a page to express visible rows, active filters/sort, selected items, a time range, a degraded-source banner, or which panel has focus. Every richer intent the north star describes ("what I am looking at") is inexpressible in the current type, on both sides of the wire.

findings.title: One of 46 shell destinations contributes any context at all
findings.evidence: frontend/src/pages/EntityDetailPage.tsx:2378-2382 (only usePageContext().set call in the tree); frontend/src/lib/shell-capability.ts:125-181 (46 capabilities)
findings.detail: grep usePageContext across frontend/src returns page-context.tsx, its test, and EntityDetailPage.tsx. All other routes — /health/*, /memory, /qa, /spend, /timeline, /entities/concentration, /ingestion/* — ship route + query params only. The chat's grounding is a per-page opt-in that 45 pages never took, with no gate that would notice.

findings.title: Sticky-routed follow-ups lose page context entirely (pinned/policy-bypass carries no context)
findings.evidence: src/butlers/core_tools/_switchboard.py:646-661 (only injector); src/butlers/api/routers/conversations.py:1601-1612 (pinned_target = routed_butler); src/butlers/modules/pipeline.py:2419-2421 (`_bypass_input = {"prompt": message_text}`, context only when source == "wellness")
findings.detail: `_build_dashboard_confirm_block` — the deterministic carrier of conversation_id AND page_context — is built inside `route_to_butler`, which only runs during LLM classification. Once a Switchboard conversation has a `routed_butler` stamped (or for any per-butler ChatPanel conversation) the envelope sets `control.pinned_target`, ingest resolves a pinned_target triage decision (roster/switchboard/tools/ingestion/ingest.py:735-752), and the pipeline takes the policy-bypass branch whose input dict is prompt-only. Message 1 may be page-grounded; messages 2..N — exactly where "and what about this one?" lives — are not.

findings.title: Page context is never persisted — not auditable, not replayable, not renderable
findings.evidence: src/butlers/api/routers/conversations.py:815-841 (_persist_dashboard_user_message passes role/content/message_id only); src/butlers/api/conversations.py:582-620 (dashboard_messages INSERT has no context column); src/butlers/api/conversation_envelope.py:124-125 (lives only in payload.raw)
findings.detail: The only durable copy of what the owner was looking at is buried inside the ingest envelope's raw payload on message_inbox, read back once by `_load_dashboard_context` (src/butlers/modules/pipeline.py:1438-1443). The transcript API cannot return it, the UI cannot show it, a retried/replayed turn cannot reconstruct it, and no audit answers "what did the butler think it was looking at when it wrote that fact?"

findings.title: No staleness semantics: the snapshot has no capture time and the consumer runs much later
findings.evidence: frontend/src/lib/page-context.tsx:148-161 (snapshot has no timestamp); frontend/src/components/chat/FloatingChatWidget.tsx:335-338 (captured at send); src/butlers/modules/pipeline.py:2856-2896 (consumed after inbox scan + classification spawn)
findings.detail: The context crosses an asynchronous queue (message_inbox → classification session → route.execute → target butler spawn). The routed butler is told the owner "was viewing" a route with no indication whether that was two seconds or twenty minutes ago, whether the page has since navigated, or whether the underlying data changed after capture. Any answer grounded in it is asserted with unearned confidence.

findings.title: No size or shape budget on a field pasted straight into two LLM prompts
findings.evidence: src/butlers/api/models/conversation.py:25-30 (query_params: dict[str, str], entity_ref: str | None, no max_length/max_items); src/butlers/modules/pipeline.py:593-597; src/butlers/core_tools/_switchboard.py:88-89
findings.detail: Both injection sites do json.dumps(page_context) with no truncation, while the surrounding envelope code does bound its other free text (_MAX_CONTEXT_CHARS, src/butlers/api/conversation_envelope.py:55-57). A long filter query string, a base64 cursor, or a verbose entity name silently inflates the classification prompt and the routed context block, with no cap, no truncation flag, and no telemetry.

findings.title: Ingested third-party data reaches the prompt unfenced
findings.evidence: frontend/src/pages/EntityDetailPage.tsx:2381 (entity_ref: entity?.canonical_name); src/butlers/modules/pipeline.py:596; src/butlers/core_tools/_switchboard.py:89
findings.detail: canonical_name is data ingested from external channels, and it lands inside the classification prompt and the routed input.context block as bare JSON — while the message body itself is deliberately fenced (<routed_message>, per the routed-message-safety contract). Page context is the one owner-adjacent channel carrying attacker-influencable strings into a prompt with no fence, no provenance label, and no "treat as data" instruction.

findings.title: The owner cannot see, review, or remove the context being attached
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/chat/MessageInput.tsx:11-28 (no context prop); frontend/src/components/chat/FloatingChatWidget.tsx:613-670 (header renders title + history/new/close only); frontend/src/components/chat/MessageThread.tsx (no context rendering)
findings.detail: Capture is entirely invisible: no chip, no tooltip, no aria description, no removal affordance, and nothing in the sent message shows what travelled with it. The north star's "the owner must SEE what context is attached before sending" has zero surface today, and the accessibility contract (announce what is attached, allow keyboard removal) has nothing to hang on.

findings.title: The butler-detail ChatPanel sends no page context at all
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/chat/ChatPanel.tsx (no page_context/pageContext occurrence anywhere in the 755-line file); src/butlers/api/routers/conversations.py:1453-1459 and 1605-1612 (both endpoints accept it)
findings.detail: The same two endpoints the floating widget uses accept page_context from the butler-detail Sheet variant, but ChatPanel never builds one. A conversation started from a butler's own page — arguably the most context-rich place in the dashboard — is grounded strictly less than the floating widget.

findings.title: No butler-side way to read what the page showed; butler DB roles cannot reach the data anyway
findings.evidence: src/butlers/api/read_models/ (activity_v1, butlers_v1, insights_v1, search_v1, sessions_v1, timeline_v1, calendar_workspace_v1 — consumed only by API routers); src/butlers/core_tools/ (no dashboard/page read tool among _switchboard/_routing/_memory_access/…); src/butlers/api/db.py:25-36 (per-butler schema-scoped pools; only the API fans out)
findings.detail: Page context is a hint the model must take on faith. There is no page_view_read-style tool, and even if a butler wanted to re-query, its role sees only its own schema plus public, so the Relationship butler cannot read the health schema behind /health/measurements. Truthful grounding for cross-domain questions can only be produced in the API process (or over the dashboard API), never inside the answering butler's own pool.

findings.title: View state that defines the question is invisible, including degraded banners
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/health/MeasurementChart.tsx:118-123 (type/since/until in URL, but windowDays and showTable in component state), 259, 337, 427 (three degraded-source boundaries)
findings.detail: Asking "why is this trending up?" from /health/measurements delivers {route: "/health/measurements", query_params: {type: …}} — the 14/30/90-day window that defines the visible trend never leaves the browser, and a chart currently rendering a measurement-trend-degraded banner is indistinguishable from a healthy one. The butler can answer confidently about data the owner can plainly see is marked degraded.

findings.title: Route is captured as a raw pathname, never resolved to the shell's own route identity
findings.evidence: frontend/src/lib/page-context.tsx:153 (route: location.pathname); frontend/src/lib/shell-capability.ts:82-97 (segmentPattern), 188-195 (resolveShellCapability), 164-172 (per-route queryWarmup naming the exact API query the page renders from)
findings.detail: The shell already owns a manifest mapping every destination to a route pattern, a human label, and the precise query the page consumes — exactly the metadata a grounded context needs — but page-context.tsx ignores it and ships /entities/8f3a… as an opaque string. Neither the classifier nor the routed butler can name the destination ("Entity detail"), recover path params, or know which read model produced what is on screen.

proposals.title: Replace PageContext with a typed ViewRef derived from the shell capability manifest
proposals.what: Retire {route, query_params, entity_ref} in favour of a ViewRef: {route_pattern, route_label, route_params, query_params, view_state, focus: [{kind,id,label}], selection: [{kind,id}], visible_range: {since,until}, degraded_sources: [string], captured_at, contract_version}. Capture resolves pattern and label via resolveShellCapability(location.pathname) instead of shipping a bare pathname; view_state is a bounded string map a page declares for state it deliberately keeps out of the URL (e.g. {window_days: "14"}). Widen PageContextEnrichment to the same typed shape so a page contributes focus, selection, visible_range, degraded_sources and view_state rather than one string. Enforce a budget in the Pydantic model: ≤32 query params, ≤512 chars per value, ≤8 focus/selection refs, ≤4 KB serialized, with server-side truncation setting truncated: true rather than silently inflating prompts.
proposals.why: Everything downstream — snapshot resolution, the prompt block, the chip, the refresh tool — needs a context object that can name a destination and its state. Today the type itself is the ceiling (page-context.tsx:45-47), while the shell already computes the missing identity (shell-capability.ts:188).
integration_points: frontend/src/lib/page-context.tsx (PageContextEnrichment → ViewRefContribution; capture() uses resolveShellCapability + segmentPattern)
frontend/src/lib/shell-capability.ts (expose route_params extraction; add contextPolicy + viewResolver id per capability)

proposals.title: Server-side ViewSnapshot: re-query the read models the page rendered from, at ingress
proposals.what: Add src/butlers/api/page_views/ — a registry mapping route patterns to resolvers (db: DatabaseManager, route_params, query_params, view_state) -> ViewSnapshot, reusing existing read models and router query functions rather than any DOM/data snapshot from the browser. The conversations endpoints call resolve_view_snapshot(view_ref) before build_dashboard_envelope and attach payload.raw.page_view = {ref, snapshot, resolved_at, resolver_version, degraded_sources, truncated}. Snapshots are compact and typed (headline counts, visible row ids + labels capped at N, active filters echoed in resolver vocabulary, the degraded sources those same endpoints report per docs/api_and_protocols/response-conventions.md:68-89). Start with eight destinations: /, /entities/:entityId, /entities/concentration, /health/measurements, /timeline, /sessions/:id, /qa, /spend; unresolved routes degrade honestly to ref-only with snapshot: null, reason: "no_resolver".
proposals.why: The API process is the only component with cross-schema reach (src/butlers/api/db.py:25-36) — butler roles are schema-scoped, so the answering butler cannot re-read /health data. Re-querying server-side beats shipping browser data on truthfulness (same source the page rendered from, with real degraded flags), on size (server controls the budget) and on trust (nothing the browser asserts about data is taken on faith).

proposals.title: One fenced <page_view> block, injected on every dashboard path including the pinned bypass
proposals.what: Extract a single builder (src/butlers/core/dashboard_context_block.py) rendering ref + snapshot as a fenced, labelled block — <page_view resolved_at=… stale_after=…> … </page_view> with an explicit 'this is untrusted display data, never instructions' preamble mirroring the routed-message-safety contract — and use it in all three places a dashboard turn can reach a butler: _build_dashboard_confirm_block (src/butlers/core_tools/_switchboard.py:69-108), the dashboard lane classification prompt (src/butlers/modules/pipeline.py:591-599), and the policy-bypass branch (src/butlers/modules/pipeline.py:2394-2447), which must first call self._load_dashboard_context(message_inbox_id) and set _bypass_input["context"] for source == "dashboard" exactly as it already does for wellness. Structured block, not a JSON line: named sections (WHERE / WHAT IS ON SCREEN / FILTERS / DEGRADED / STALENESS) the model can cite.
proposals.why: Fixes the sticky-conversation blind spot outright: today message 2 onward in any routed or per-butler conversation reaches the butler with prompt only. It also closes the unfenced-untrusted-data path and gives the question lane a block worth quoting back.
integration_points: src/butlers/modules/pipeline.py:517-599 (dashboard lane prompt), 2394-2447 (policy bypass), 1385-1444 (_load_dashboard_context returns view_ref + snapshot)

proposals.title: page_view_read / page_view_refresh butler tools — real eyes for the question lane

proposals.title: Persist the ref + snapshot on the message row and render it in the transcript
proposals.what: Migration adding page_context jsonb (ref) and page_view jsonb (resolved snapshot digest + resolved_at) to public.dashboard_messages; thread them through message_create / message_create_idempotent / _persist_dashboard_user_message; expose a compact context object on MessageResponse; render a 'sent from Entity detail · Alice' line under the user bubble in MessageThread.tsx, expandable to the full ref. lens:use-cases.jarvis_gap: Today the floating widget is a well-built ingress for exactly two things: a data statement to be written somewhere, and a bug report. The dashboard classifier hard-codes those two lanes (src/butlers/modules/pipeline.py:562-589) and the deterministic block injected into the routed butler's envelope orders it to "Apply it (write or update the relevant fact/record)" (src/butlers/core_tools/_switchboard.py:97-99) — so the most common JARVIS utterance, a question about what is on screen, is structurally impossible: it is either forced into a write lane or forced to `general` as a best guess (pipeline.py:576-579). Even if a question lane existed, the butler would have nothing to answer from: page_context is {route, query_params, entity_ref} (frontend/src/lib/page-context.tsx:148-161), exactly one of ~45 routes enriches it (frontend/src/pages/EntityDetailPage.tsx:2378), there is no notion of the row or selection the owner is pointing at (PageContextEnrichment has one optional field, page-context.tsx:46), and the chat front door cannot even ask a peer — delegate_ask is gated off staffers (src/butlers/core_tools/_delegation.py:262) and Switchboard is a staffer (roster/switchboard/butler.toml). Acting is worse: whole domains the dashboard exposes (spend ceilings, model routing, connector pause, filter rules, notification snooze) have zero MCP tool surface anywhere in src/butlers/, so "pause email ingestion until Monday" has no butler to land in. And the chat cannot touch the page back — SSE emits only dispatch_accepted/token/message_complete/error/done (src/butlers/api/routers/conversations.py:692,798-799) and no chat component imports a navigator — so navigate/find, filter-this-list, and highlight-that-row are off the table by construction. The distance to the north star is not polish: it is three missing organs (a read/ask lane, a truthful view of page contents, and an operator tool surface) plus a return channel from chat to page.

There is no third branch, and no branch that answers without a side effect. This is the single largest structural blocker for the owner's directive; it is also the cheapest place to fix it (one function, `_build_dashboard_lane_prompt`).

findings.evidence: src/butlers/core_tools/_switchboard.py:84-107, esp. line 97 "1. Interpret the statement against your own domain schema/predicates." and line 98 "2. Apply it (write or update the relevant fact/record)."

Because the classifier has no question lane, "who is this person and when did I last talk to them?" arrives at the Relationship butler with an unconditional instruction to interpret and apply it. The failure mode is not a bad answer — it is a fabricated fact written to the entity graph and then confirmed back to the owner as recorded truth. A correctness hazard, not merely a UX gap.

ux:a11y-keyboard.jarvis_gap: The widget has real accessibility engineering underneath it — a shared focus-choreography hook, a pre-stream aria-live status line, a global reduced-motion floor, and an sr-only Stop-status announcer — but the single flow that matters most for a JARVIS voice (hearing what the butler actually said) is silent to screen-reader users: the streamed reply text is never placed in a live region and, once committed, lands in a plain static bubble a screen reader will not proactively announce. Layered on top, the widget has no dedicated global keyboard entry point (only a two-step Ctrl+K-then-type-then-Enter path, unlike '?' and 'g' which get real bare-key bindings), and its deliberate non-modal focus policy (trapFocus:false) has no guard against WCAG 2.2's new 2.4.11 Focus-Not-Obscured requirement, since the fixed panel floats over page content that remains fully tabbable underneath it. None of this is a redesign-scale problem — each is a bounded, well-scoped fix inside files that already show the right instincts — but as shipped, a screen-reader-only or keyboard-only owner cannot actually converse with the JARVIS voice: they can send a message and never learn what came back without manually re-navigating into the thread.

findings.title: Streamed and committed reply content is never announced to screen readers
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/chat/MessageThread.tsx:369-403 wraps only the pre-first-token pendingActivityStatus text in role="status" aria-live="polite" (line 373-374); the streaming bubble at lines 385-403 (SimpleMarkdown content={streaming.content}) has no aria-live ancestor, and once message_complete fires the text becomes a static MessageBubble (line 356) with no live region at all.
findings.detail: A screen-reader user hears "Routed to X; waiting for a reply" and then nothing — not the incoming tokens, not the finished answer. For a product whose north star is a JARVIS voice that answers questions, this makes the core answer-delivery path non-functional for non-visual users. This is a WCAG 2.2 AA gap (4.1.3 Status Messages) on the highest-traffic content in the panel.

findings.title: No dedicated global keyboard shortcut to open/focus the chat widget
findings.evidence: frontend/src/hooks/use-keyboard-shortcuts.ts:14-72 binds only Cmd/Ctrl+K (entity finder), '/' (entity finder), '?' (shortcut help, line 45-49), and 'g'+key chords sourced from G_CHORD_ROUTES (route-registry). FloatingChatWidget.tsx:781-792 only reaches the palette command 'talk-to-butlers' — there is no bare-key or event-listener binding analogous to OPEN_SHORTCUT_HELP_EVENT (shortcut-help.ts, wired at shortcut-hints.tsx:82-88).
findings.detail: Opening chat today requires Ctrl+K (or '/') -> type "talk to butlers" or "chat" -> Enter, a 3-4 keystroke discovery path, and it does not exist as a listed row in shortcut-hints.tsx's STATIC_SHORTCUTS (lines 20-24), so it is not even discoverable in the '?' help sheet. A JARVIS voice meant to be reachable 'from any page' deserves the same first-class binding '?' has, not a buried palette entry.

findings.title: trapFocus:false leaves page content behind the fixed panel fully tabbable and visually obscured (WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.11)
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/chat/FloatingChatWidget.tsx:131-136 sets trapFocus:false on useModalChoreography with the comment 'deliberately leaves page tab order available'; the panel itself is `fixed bottom-20 right-4 z-40 ... h-[min(560px,70vh)] w-[min(380px,calc(100vw-2rem))]` (line 607). RootLayout.tsx never reserves right/bottom padding for it (only the mount at line 126, no padding/margin adjustment).
findings.detail: The non-modal pattern itself (role="dialog" without aria-modal) is the right instinct per WAI-ARIA APG, but nothing stops Tab from moving focus to a page element that sits underneath the panel's 380x560px footprint (e.g. a table row action, pagination control, or footer link near the bottom-right of a scrolled page) while it remains rendered on top -- WCAG 2.2's new SC 2.4.11 requires the focused component not be entirely hidden by author-created content. As implemented there is no inert/skip-past guard and no scroll-into-view correction for an obscured focus target.

findings.title: Auto-scroll bypasses the project's own reduced-motion floor
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/chat/MessageThread.tsx:303-306 calls bottomRef.current?.scrollIntoView({ behavior: "smooth" }); index.css:787-796 sets `scroll-behavior: auto !important` under prefers-reduced-motion, but the CSSOM View spec has explicit `behavior:'smooth'` on scrollIntoView override the CSS `scroll-behavior` property.
findings.detail: Every new token/message triggers a smooth-scroll animation that the project's own documented reduced-motion floor (index.css:773-786, 'motion restraint becomes the default, not a per-component courtesy') does not actually reach, because it is invoked as an explicit JS option rather than relying on CSS. Minor individually, but it is exactly the kind of animation-from-interaction that a vestibular-sensitive owner would expect the floor to catch, and it fires continuously during every streamed reply.

findings.title: Header icon controls (History/New/Back/Close) sit at the bare 24x24 WCAG floor, packed 2px apart
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/chat/FloatingChatWidget.tsx:627-669 uses size="icon-xs" for all four header buttons; button.tsx:29 defines icon-xs as `size-6` (24x24px), and the container at FloatingChatWidget.tsx:624 uses `gap-0.5` (2px) between them.
findings.detail: 24x24 exactly meets WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8's AA minimum but sits well below the Apple HIG/Material 44x44/48dp touch guidance the project's own accessibility skill cites as the ergonomic floor. On a touch device these are the widget's session-ending controls (New conversation discards the thread state, Close dismisses the panel) placed 2px from a merely-navigational History button -- a mis-tap risk concentrated in the one entry point meant to be frictionless from every page.

findings.title: Fixed-position panel height (70vh) is not keyboard-viewport-aware on mobile
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/chat/FloatingChatWidget.tsx:607 sizes the panel `h-[min(560px,70vh)]` with `fixed bottom-20 right-4`; no `100dvh`/`100svh` unit or `window.visualViewport` resize listener appears anywhere in the file.
findings.detail: On iOS Safari and many Android browsers, a `fixed`-positioned element sized against the layout viewport does not reflow when the on-screen keyboard opens (the visual viewport shrinks but `vh` does not) -- the MessageInput textarea at the panel's bottom can end up covered by, or occluded near, the keyboard on phones. This is exactly the mobile touch-ergonomics failure mode the lens calls out; it needs verification on a real device/simulator but is a well-known pattern-level defect given the current CSS.

proposals.title: Give the assistant reply a real off-screen aria-live channel, decoupled from the visible per-token bubble
proposals.what: In MessageThread.tsx, add a visually-hidden (`sr-only`) `<div role="status" aria-live="polite" aria-atomic="false">` sibling to the message list. Do NOT feed it every token event. Instead: (a) buffer streaming.content and flush a new child span into the live region only at sentence/paragraph boundaries (split on /[.!?]\s/ or a ~1.5s idle timer, whichever fires first) so screen readers get incremental, non-interrupting announcements instead of per-token spam; (b) on message_complete, flush any remaining buffered text and append one final 'Reply complete' marker only if the reply took over ~3s. Keep the existing visible SimpleMarkdown bubble unchanged -- it stays the sighted-user rendering; the live region is purely the SR channel, mirroring the sr-only stopStatus pattern already used correctly in MessageInput.tsx:66-70.
proposals.why: This is the single highest-value a11y fix: it is the difference between a screen-reader user being able to use the JARVIS voice at all versus not. The sentence-boundary/idle-flush throttle is the standard pattern for making a token stream perceivable without being unusable noise -- a raw per-token aria-live region is worse than no announcement at all because it interrupts speech mid-word on every update.

ux:conversation-surface.jarvis_gap: Today the "Talk to Butlers" surface is a 380x560 shadcn messenger popover bolted to the bottom-right corner: it streams honestly, it can be stopped, it classifies send errors, and it quietly attaches a route snapshot — real reliability work. But as a conversation surface it is not designed to this project's own language and cannot do what the north star asks. It cannot render an answer: `SimpleMarkdown` (MessageThread.tsx:46) splits code fences and dumps everything else as literal text, so a table, a bullet list, or a bare URL in a butler's reply arrives as raw markdown source with no clickable link — and the message contract has no citation field at all (models/conversation.py:100), so the drill-down spine that makes this dashboard worth having simply terminates at the chat bubble. It cannot show the owner what it is looking at: page context is captured invisibly at send time (FloatingChatWidget.tsx:338), is unremovable, and is empty on every route but one (only EntityDetailPage.tsx:2378 enriches), so the promise "converse about what you are looking at" is currently a promise about the URL string. It cannot be worked in: the composer is disabled while a turn runs (MessageInput.tsx:77), drafts die when the popover unmounts (FloatingChatWidget.tsx:823), there are no suggested prompts, no slash commands, no direct keyboard route, and the empty state is one generic sentence that teaches none of the lanes the backend actually requires (pipeline.py:560). It cannot be lived in: one cramped posture exists, history is a full takeover of the same narrow column, in-thread links are `target="_blank"` full page loads that throw the conversation away (MessageThread.tsx:209), and a second near-duplicate 755-line implementation runs the same state machine on butler detail (ChatPanel.tsx:742). And visually it contradicts Dispatch on nearly every count that matters — a drop-shadowed card, a round primary-fill FAB, 16px-radius chat bubbles with fill backgrounds, `animate-bounce` dots, non-tabular numbers. The distance to JARVIS is not a feature gap; it is that the surface was built as a chat widget attached to a dashboard rather than as the dashboard's voice.

findings.title: Assistant answers cannot render structure — headings, lists, tables, bold, and links all arrive as literal markdown source

findings.detail:
SimpleMarkdown splits only on fenced code blocks and renders every other part as a `

This is the single largest blocker to the question-answering lane the 2026-09-02 directive asks for: the lane can be built end to end and the answer will still be unreadable. It also violates the Dispatch type system (spec.md § Type System) — assistant prose is the system's Voice and should carry the serif/mono split, but every reply currently renders in one 14px sans blob.

The dashboard's whole value is the drill-down spine (docs/frontend/purpose-and-single-pane.md § Detect/Diagnose/Act); the chat surface currently cuts it. findings.title: The empty state teaches nothing, and the lanes the backend requires are invisible
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/chat/MessageThread.tsx:332-338 ("No messages yet. Start the conversation below."); src/butlers/modules/pipeline.py:560-585 (two-lane classification prompt: data statement vs bug report)
findings.detail: The backend forces every dashboard message into Lane A (route to a domain butler) or Lane B (file a bug), and tells the classifier to guess Lane A when uncertain (pipeline.py:576-580). The owner is never shown that this taxonomy exists, so a question — the lane the 2026-09-02 directive now wants — is silently classified as a statement to route. Even after the question lane is built, the surface has to teach three lanes; today it teaches zero. It is also a Dispatch copy violation: the page-level empty-state model (spec.md § Interface Copy) requires a `{Noun} + verb phrase` title plus at most one sentence and one action, not a lone instruction sentence.

findings.title: No per-message answer attribution: the thread never says which butler spoke
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/chat/MessageThread.tsx:177-231 (meta row: time, model, tokens, ms, cost, two links — no butler); ConversationHeader.tsx:61 deliberately scopes attribution to the live turn only; ConversationSummary.routed_butler exists and is rendered in the list at ConversationList.tsx:93-101
findings.detail: Reopen a past conversation and the header reads "switchboard" with no route, and no individual reply carries its author. In a multi-butler system where different messages in one thread can be answered by different specialists, the thread is the one place attribution matters and it is the one place it is absent. Dispatch also requires butler identity to render as a ButlerMark letter-mark (spec.md § Butler Letter-Mark); no ButlerMark appears anywhere in frontend/src/components/chat/.

findings.title: Only one cramped posture exists, and a second near-duplicate implementation runs beside it
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/chat/FloatingChatWidget.tsx:607 (`h-[min(560px,70vh)] w-[min(380px,calc(100vw-2rem))]`, no resize); :673-687 (history replaces the thread via viewMode); frontend/src/components/chat/ChatPanel.tsx:742 (a separate 480px Sheet, 755 lines duplicating the same SSE/stop/reconcile machine)
findings.detail: A 380px overlay anchored over the bottom-right of the page you are asking about is the worst posture for page-context conversation: it covers content, it cannot show a table or a citation list, and history is a full takeover of the same narrow column so you lose your place going back. There is no docked panel that keeps the page visible, and no full-page route for long answers or for searching history. Meanwhile ChatPanel.tsx maintains a parallel copy of the turn state machine — every reliability fix has to land twice.

findings.title: Dispatch conformance: the chat surface is a card with a drop shadow, a round fill CTA, and fill-background bubbles
findings.evidence: FloatingChatWidget.tsx:607 (`rounded-lg border bg-card shadow-lg`); :807 (`size-12 rounded-full p-0 shadow-lg`, variant default = `bg-primary`, button.tsx:12); MessageThread.tsx:134-142 (`rounded-2xl px-4 py-2.5`, `bg-primary text-primary-foreground`)
findings.detail: Violates Composure Doctrine rule 3 ("Surfaces, not cards"), Anti-Pattern Prohibitions ("drop shadows on cards — there are no cards"), and Button Forms (exactly three forms: action arrow, pill, commit; "The system has no rounded gradient CTA anywhere"). Bubble radius 16px has no basis in the language's 3-4px radius vocabulary. This is the most-seen surface in the product and it is the least Dispatch-conformant one; per spec.md § Page Conformance check 10 it does not read like the Overview.

findings.title: Forbidden motion: bouncing typing dots and unguarded smooth scroll
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/chat/TypingIndicator.tsx:14-22 (`animate-bounce` x3 with staggered delays); MessageThread.tsx:305 (`scrollIntoView({ behavior: "smooth" })`)
findings.detail: Motion Vocabulary lists exactly four permitted animations and explicitly forbids bounce. The staggered three-dot bounce is a chat-app cliche, not a state signal — and the surface already has a truthful text status right above it (MessageThread.tsx:369-381), so the dots carry no information at all. Smooth scroll is outside the vocabulary and is not gated on prefers-reduced-motion at the call site (index.css:793 has a global reduced-motion clamp, but the behavior:"smooth" JS option is not a CSS transition and is not covered by it).

findings.title: Numbers in the thread are neither mono nor tabular
findings.evidence: MessageThread.tsx:193-205 (`{input_tokens}+{output_tokens} tokens`, `{duration_ms}ms`, cost string — all plain `text-xs text-muted-foreground`); ConversationHeader.tsx:82 (`· ~$0.0004`)
findings.detail: Dispatch § Tabular Numerals requires every numeric value to render tabular-nums, and numeric facts (IDs, timestamps, deltas, costs) to use the mono family. The chat meta row streams changing token counts and durations in proportional sans, so digits jitter as they update. The `Mono` primitive (frontend/src/components/ui/Mono.tsx) already exists and is unused here.

findings.title: The meta row stacks five competing affordances under every reply
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/chat/MessageThread.tsx:177-231 — relative time, model badge, token count, duration, cost, session icon-link, "View lineage" text link, all in one wrapping flex row
findings.detail: Seven signals with equal muted weight under every answer, in a 380px column where they wrap to three lines. Dispatch § Composure Doctrine rule 5 is one affordance per signal; design-bar's density bias asks what mode the user is in — reading an answer, not auditing token spend. The audit facts belong behind one disclosure or on the /chat and session surfaces, with at most a single action-arrow to provenance in the thread.

findings.title: No direct keyboard route to the system's primary voice; opening it costs an extra Tab

Dispatch/design-bar bias 7 says frequent paths grow shortcut routes, and this is meant to be the most frequent path in the product. Opening a chat surface should land the caret in the composer; focusing the title is correct dialog choreography for a modal but wrong for a surface whose only purpose is typing.

findings.title: Conversation search is a 28px box inside a 380px popover, behind a mode switch, with no snippets
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/chat/ConversationList.tsx:241-264 (h-7 input, `placeholder="Search..."`); results render as title + relative time only at :88-102; reachable in the widget only after clicking History (FloatingChatWidget.tsx:629-636)

findings.title: The unread badge is silent to assistive tech and the dialog role is asserted without modality
findings.evidence: FloatingChatWidget.tsx:814-820 (badge is `aria-hidden`, state folded into the trigger's aria-label at :809 — correct, but no live region announces arrival); FloatingChatWidget.tsx:133-136 (`useModalChoreography({ onClose, trapFocus: false })`) with `role="dialog"` at :607 and no aria-modal

findings.title: Interface copy drifts from the Dispatch voice

Backend design of the question-answering lane through the Switchboard spine — reported only as its UI-visible consequence (the lanes are invisible and untaught); the lane's classifier and routing design belongs to the routing lens

lens:question-lane-tools.jarvis_gap: Today a dashboard question has exactly two exits, and both are wrong. The classification prompt (`src/butlers/modules/pipeline.py:559-589`) offers a closed two-lane taxonomy — `route_to_butler` (data statement/correction) or `file_bug_report` (bug) — and the structured fast-lane schema (`roster/switchboard/tools/routing/structured_classify.py:81-140`) mirrors exactly those two tools. Worse, the prompt explicitly instructs the model that when it cannot classify, it must "still call `route_to_butler` with the best-guess specialist (or `general`)" (`pipeline.py:576-580`) — the silent-route-to-General the 2026-07-28 dossier forbids, encoded as a normative instruction. And the contract the routed butler then receives is a *mutation* contract: "Interpret the statement… Apply it (write or update the relevant fact/record)… confirm" (`src/butlers/core_tools/_switchboard.py:90-107`). So "how much did I spend on models this week?" is dispatched to a domain butler that has been told to write something, or to the General butler whose MANIFESTO is a storage second brain (`roster/general/MANIFESTO.md`) with no fleet visibility at all. Meanwhile nothing in the MCP plane can see the data the dashboard shows: `sessions_*` core tools are per-butler-pool and staffer-excluded (`src/butlers/core_tools/_sessions.py:50`), so the Switchboard has none, and the cross-butler read boundary that actually powers the dashboard — `src/butlers/api/read_models/{sessions_v1,butlers_v1,search_v1,timeline_v1,activity_v1,insights_v1}.py` — exists only inside the FastAPI process, invisible to every LLM session. On top of that, every dashboard turn pays two cold CLI spawns (classification + target), because the in-process structured fast lane is explicitly gated off for `source == "dashboard"` (`pipeline.py:2954-2958`) on Stop-registration grounds, against a 300 s SSE timeout (`src/butlers/api/routers/conversations.py:168`) sized for an agentic write session. The distance to JARVIS is therefore not "add a chat model": it is (a) a third lane with a read-only answer contract, (b) a named owner holding a real fleet read toolkit under an RFC-0010-class exception, (c) a latency budget where a read-only question does not cost two subprocess spawns, and (d) a first-class truthful "I cannot see that" terminal that is neither a QA bug nor a route to General.

findings.title: The lane taxonomy is closed at two, and both exits mutate or file bugs
findings.evidence: src/butlers/modules/pipeline.py:559-589 (`_build_dashboard_lane_prompt`: "Decide which of TWO LANES"… "You MUST call exactly one of `route_to_butler` or `file_bug_report`"); roster/switchboard/tools/routing/structured_classify.py:81-140 (only ROUTE_TO_BUTLER_TOOL and FILE_BUG_REPORT_TOOL schemas exist)
findings.detail: There is no tool a classification session can call that means "the owner asked a question". Because the prompt forces exactly one of two calls and the forced-tool-use schema offers exactly those two, a question is structurally coerced into a mutation dispatch or a QA finding. The lane-exclusivity guard (`src/butlers/core_tools/_switchboard.py:42-43`, `:502-533`) is built for exactly two lanes and will need a third claim value.

findings.title: The classification prompt normatively instructs the forbidden route-to-General fallback
findings.evidence: src/butlers/modules/pipeline.py:576-580: "If the message is genuinely ambiguous or you cannot classify it into either lane, still call `route_to_butler` with the best-guess specialist (or `general`) rather than calling nothing — an unrouted dashboard message leaves the owner's chat waiting with no reply."

findings.title: General butler cannot answer anything the dashboard shows
findings.evidence: roster/general/MANIFESTO.md ("The General Butler does one thing well: remember"); roster/general/butler.toml modules = calendar, contacts, general, memory (groups core/preferences/entity), steam

findings.title: The injected routed-butler contract is a write contract, unsafe for questions
findings.evidence: src/butlers/core_tools/_switchboard.py:69-108 (`_build_dashboard_confirm_block`): "1. Interpret the statement against your own domain schema/predicates. 2. Apply it (write or update the relevant fact/record). 3. Call the `conversation_reply` MCP tool…"; injected unconditionally for every dashboard route at :646-661
findings.detail: This block is appended deterministically to every dashboard `route_to_butler` envelope regardless of intent. A question routed today arrives at a domain butler carrying an explicit instruction to write a record. findings.title: One timeout budget for two very different lanes

proposals.title: RFC 0012: a system-plane read exception, the doctrinal unlock the Concierge needs
proposals.what: Write `about/legends-and-lore/rfcs/0012-system-plane-read-exception.md` extending the RFC 0010 exception class from briefing state to fleet *operational telemetry*, and land `concierge.v_fleet_sessions` / `concierge.v_fleet_spend` as read-only UNION views over each butler schema's `sessions` table, created by an Alembic migration under roster/concierge/migrations with explicit cross-schema SELECT grants. Carry RFC 0010's five guardrails verbatim plus a sixth: a **column allowlist** — id, butler (hardcoded literal per UNION term), started_at, ended_at, status, trigger_source, model, input_tokens, output_tokens, cost_cents, error_class. Prompt and result text are NOT in the view; a question about a specific session's content routes as a domain question to that butler instead.
proposals.why: `read_models` fan out across N per-butler pools held by the dashboard's `DatabaseManager` (src/butlers/api/read_models/sessions_v1.py:19-28, butlers_v1.py:14). So a Concierge tool cannot call read_models as written, and the three honest options are: fan out via Switchboard (13 LLM sessions to answer 'what did we spend today' — precisely the cost ratio RFC 0010 rejected at 9:1), mount an MCP server inside the FastAPI process (no daemon, no session log, no spend accounting, no Stop), or extend the sanctioned view exception. The third is the only one that keeps the MCP-only rule intact where it matters — no writes cross schemas, no butler imports another's module, no interactive cross-schema query — while making the cost argument explicitly, in writing, subject to review. Do not skip this and quietly add cross-schema grants: the RFC is the artifact that keeps the exception bounded.

ux:speed-streaming.jarvis_gap: A JARVIS voice must feel instant to establish presence — the first perceptible response (even just 'heard you, thinking') should land in well under a second, and the reply itself should render as it is produced. Today's chat loop does neither: dashboard messages are deliberately excluded from the fast structured-classification lane (pipeline.py:2957, source != "dashboard"), so every single dashboard turn pays for two full sequential CLI/Agent-SDK session spawns (a classify spawn, then a routed-butler spawn) before a byte of the answer exists anywhere; and even once the answer exists, the backend does not stream it — it polls the database every 500ms (conversations.py:165 _POLL_INTERVAL_S) until the routed butler's session has fully finished and persisted conversation_reply, then emits the entire reply as one token SSE event (conversations.py:798). The frontend's "streaming" architecture (per-token content accumulation in FloatingChatWidget.tsx:401-411, markdown-safe incremental rendering in MessageThread.tsx) is real, tested plumbing wired to a source that never sends more than one chunk. Closing this gap requires the target butler's own token generation to be forwarded live (not polled-for-completion), and it requires the dashboard channel to get a real fast path to first activity that does not require Stop durability to come from a second full spawn.

findings.title: No real token streaming — the whole reply arrives as one SSE 'token' event
findings.evidence: src/butlers/api/routers/conversations.py:789-798 — the poll loop waits for message_find_reply_since to return a fully-persisted row, then does `yield _sse_event("token", {"content": reply_row["content"]})` exactly once, immediately followed by message_complete and done.
findings.detail: The SSE docstring (lines 57-64) describes 'token' as a streamed unit, and the frontend is built to accumulate tokens incrementally (content: prev.content + token, FloatingChatWidget.tsx:406-410), but the backend never emits more than one token chunk per turn. This is polling-for-completion dressed as streaming: the owner sees nothing until the routed butler's entire agentic session (which may include multiple tool calls) has finished end-to-end, then the full answer appears at once.

findings.title: Dashboard channel is explicitly excluded from the fast classification lane, forcing two full sequential CLI spawns before any work starts

Fallback is `spawn_result = await self._dispatch_fn(**dispatch_kwargs)` at line 2998, a full CLI/Agent-SDK session spawn.

findings.title: No stream reconnect — a tab sleep or network blip drops the read and the client reports a hard failure even though the server-side turn likely still completes
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/chat/FloatingChatWidget.tsx uses fetch + response.body.getReader() via consumeSseStream (sse-utils.ts:45-81), not EventSource. On any non-AbortError during the read, FloatingChatWidget.tsx:471-481 hits the else branch: setStreaming(...null); setSendError({kind: "generic", message: "Failed to send message.", ...}).
findings.detail: fetch's ReadableStream has no built-in reconnect/Last-Event-ID semantics (unlike EventSource), so a phone lock, laptop sleep, or Wi-Fi blip surfaces as a flat 'Failed to send message' even though the backend generator only exits early on request.is_disconnected() (conversations.py:707-709) while the routed butler's own session, once dispatched, runs to completion independently and still writes conversation_reply. There is no refetch-and-reconcile of messages after this failure path; the owner must manually reopen/refresh to discover the answer landed.

findings.title: Auto-scroll uses scrollIntoView({behavior:"smooth"}) on every content mutation — latent jank once real per-token streaming lands
findings.evidence: MessageThread.tsx:303-316 — the effect depends on streaming?.content (among others) and calls bottomRef.current?.scrollIntoView({behavior:"smooth"}) on every change; handleScroll (MessageThread.tsx:295-300) tracks userScrolledUp correctly but the scroll trigger itself is not throttled.
findings.detail: Invisible today because streaming.content only changes once per turn (finding #1). Once real per-token streaming exists, dozens of smooth-scroll calls per second would queue/interrupt each other and force repeated layout reads via scrollHeight.

proposals.title: Give dashboard chat a real fast path: structured/direct classification without sacrificing Stop durability
proposals.what: Redesign the dashboard classify step so it no longer requires a full CLI spawn purely to uphold the Stop guarantee: register the durable Spawner-tracked runtime row before calling the lightweight structured classifier (the same try_structured_classification fast lane already used for non-dashboard channels) so Stop still has a session row to address, but classification hits the local MCP tool-call adapter instead of a second full CLI process. Fall back to a full CLI classify spawn only when the structured lane can't produce a decision, mirroring the existing non-dashboard fallback at pipeline.py:2996-2998.
proposals.why: This is the single biggest latency source identified — two sequential full agent-process cold starts before any user-visible progress. The current dashboard exclusion (pipeline.py:2957) trades speed for a Stop-durability property that can likely be satisfied by pre-registering the session row instead.
integration_points: src/butlers/core/dashboard_turns.py (open_turn / claim_ingress — pre-registration point for Stop)

proposals.title: Stream real tokens from the routed butler's own session into the SSE response instead of polling for the finished row
proposals.what: Replace the poll-for-completed-row pattern in _stream_conversation_response (conversations.py:700-798) with live forwarding: have the routed butler's runtime publish incremental token/delta events (e.g. Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY on a per-request-id channel, or a shared async queue keyed by request_id) that the SSE generator subscribes to and forwards as multiple token events as they arrive, falling back to the current single-shot emission when the target butler doesn't support streaming output.
proposals.why: This is the core promise of 'SSE streaming' that the current implementation only simulates. Without it, no frontend polish makes chat feel like a live conversation — the owner always waits for the entire answer, then sees a paste-in.
integration_points: the routed butler's runtime spawner path receiving Agent SDK streaming callbacks (trace from pipeline.py _dispatch_fn)
new pub/sub primitive: Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY per request_id, or an in-process broker
frontend already ready to consume this: FloatingChatWidget.tsx:401-411 needs no change

proposals.title: Add phase-aware progress status instead of two static strings
proposals.what: Extend dispatch_accepted-style receipts (or add a new lightweight SSE event) to report phase transitions the backend already knows about: classifying -> routed to {butler}, starting session -> thinking (tool: {name}) as tool calls happen -> writing reply. Surface these in pendingActivityStatus (MessageThread.tsx:275-281) instead of the current two-string function, and consider surfacing in-flight tool call names live.
proposals.why: Even before token-level streaming lands (proposal 2), truthful, changing status text turns a multi-second silent wait into a legible one — serves the north star's honesty-about-routing requirement and reduces perceived latency without reducing actual latency.
integration_points: src/butlers/api/routers/conversations.py (emit new phase events from the poll loop / session lifecycle hooks)
frontend/src/components/chat/ToolCallDetails.tsx (reuse for live in-flight tool calls, not just post-hoc)

proposals.title: Make the client stream connection reconnect/recover instead of failing hard on a network blip
proposals.what: Either switch to native EventSource (auto-reconnect + Last-Event-ID) with the SSE endpoint emitting a resumable event id, or keep fetch+ReadableStream but wrap the consume loop so that, on a non-AbortError failure, it first refetches GET .../messages for the conversation to check whether conversation_reply already landed before surfacing any 'failed' state.
proposals.why: Directly answers the lens's tab-sleep/network-blip question. A transient network hiccup currently produces a false 'Failed to send message' even when the backend turn completed successfully seconds later — a truthfulness/trust problem as much as a UX one.
integration_points: frontend/src/hooks/use-conversations.ts (refetchMessages already exists and could be invoked from the failure path)

proposals.title: Shorten/replace the DB poll interval with an event-driven wake
proposals.what: As an incremental step ahead of proposal 2, replace the fixed 500ms asyncio.sleep(_POLL_INTERVAL_S) poll (conversations.py:789-793) with a Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY wake on conversation_reply insert for the given conversation, falling back to a short poll as a safety net.
proposals.why: Small, cheap latency win (up to 500ms) shippable independently of the bigger spawn-serialization fix, and it's the same primitive proposal 2 would need anyway.
integration_points: wherever conversation_reply_create persists the assistant message — add a NOTIFY there

proposals.title: Throttle the streaming auto-scroll trigger ahead of real token streaming landing
proposals.what: Change the scroll-on-content-change effect in MessageThread.tsx to throttle via requestAnimationFrame or a small interval (e.g. max once per 100-150ms) rather than firing scrollIntoView({behavior:"smooth"}) on every streaming.content change.
proposals.why: Pure preventive fix — invisible today (single-shot content), but would visibly jank the moment proposal 2 ships real per-token updates. Cheap to do now alongside the streaming work so it isn't a regression discovered later.

lens:actions-from-chat.jarvis_gap: Today the chat widget is a one-way statement pipe: the owner types, the Switchboard classifies into exactly two lanes (data-statement or bug-report, `src/butlers/modules/pipeline.py:563-576`), the routed butler is instructed to APPLY the change and then narrate it (`src/butlers/core_tools/_switchboard.py:97-103`), and the only channel back into the thread is a plain string (`src/butlers/core_tools/_conversation_reply.py:59-119`). There is not one interactive control in the entire chat tree — `MessageThread.tsx` renders bubbles plus a read-only JSON tool-call disclosure and nothing else. So the owner cannot confirm, cannot deny, cannot undo, cannot see whether the thing actually ran, and cannot get from a thread reply to the dashboard row where the effect is visible. Worse, the "ask the owner to confirm" step is theatre: the write already landed before the question was asked, which inverts the security doctrine that approval gates "pause execution and request explicit owner confirmation before proceeding" (`about/heart-and-soul/security.md:103-105`). Meanwhile every piece needed for a real command surface already exists and is unwired: a vetted `pending_actions` queue with a decision dossier (why / evidence / blast_radius / reversibility), an audited approve/deny/defer/retry/abandon endpoint family, a shared optimistic-mutation + 5-second-undo hook, an at-most-once external-effect claim in the dashboard turn ledger, and a startup-validated exact-argument command registry. JARVIS is the distance between "the butler tells you it did something" and "the butler proposes something, you press Confirm in the thread, it flows through the same authority as the page button, and the thread shows you an honest receipt with a link to where the effect lives" — and that distance is currently one hundred percent of the way.

findings.title: The chat thread has zero action affordances — it is render-only by construction
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/chat/MessageThread.tsx:126-235 (MessageBubble renders content, error, cancel state, metadata links only); frontend/src/components/chat/ToolCallDetails.tsx:84-118 (a read-only collapsible JSON dump); frontend/src/components/chat/FloatingChatWidget.tsx:373-439 (SSE switch handles conversation_created/dispatch_accepted/token/message_complete/error/done)
findings.detail: No button, card, form, or confirm control exists anywhere under frontend/src/components/chat/. Every one of the 5,784 lines in that tree is about getting text in and text out. A chat-initiated action therefore has no place to land in the UI even if the backend proposed one.

findings.title: conversation_reply is a text-only wire — an action proposal has no way to reach the thread
findings.evidence: src/butlers/core_tools/_conversation_reply.py:59-77 (signature is exactly `conversation_id: str, message: str`); src/butlers/core_tools/_switchboard.py:99-105 (the deterministic block names conversation_reply as the ONLY way the owner sees anything)
findings.detail: This is the single sanctioned channel from a routed butler session back into public.dashboard_messages. It accepts no structured payload, no action reference, no tool-call list. Any structured proposal must either extend this tool or add a sibling — there is no third option, because the SSE poller (`message_find_reply_since`) only watches for rows this tool writes.

findings.title: conversation_reply_create silently drops session_id and tool_calls, making two spec requirements permanently unsatisfiable
findings.evidence: src/butlers/api/conversations.py:721-727 (message_create called with only conversation_id/role/content/request_id); src/butlers/api/conversations.py:564-582 (message_create accepts session_id, tool_calls, model_name, duration_ms — all defaulted to None here); openspec/specs/dashboard-chat-ui/spec.md:80-86 and :284-291
findings.detail: Every assistant message in every dashboard conversation has session_id NULL and tool_calls NULL. Consequently MessageThread.tsx:170-174 (tool-call section) and :208-218 (session drill-down link) are dead code, the spec's 'Tool call visibility' and 'Session link on assistant message' scenarios can never pass against the real path, and — most damaging for this lens — pending_actions.session_id (indexed at src/butlers/modules/approvals/migrations/001_approvals_tables.py:85-88) can never be joined back to the chat message whose turn parked it.

findings.title: Act-then-ask: the routed-butler contract mandates applying the change BEFORE asking for confirmation
findings.evidence: src/butlers/core_tools/_switchboard.py:97-103 — "1. Interpret the statement… 2. Apply it (write or update the relevant fact/record). 3. Call the `conversation_reply` MCP tool … asking the owner to confirm"; contradicts about/heart-and-soul/security.md:103-105
findings.detail: The owner's 'correct?' prompt arrives after the mutation is durable. There is no propose state, so a wrong interpretation is already persisted when the owner reads it, and the only remedy is a second corrective turn. This is the single deepest design obstacle to a command surface: the system currently has no concept of a proposed-but-unexecuted chat action.

findings.title: Two live approve endpoints with different authority semantics — one audits, one does not
findings.evidence: src/butlers/api/routers/approvals.py:930-999 (POST /api/approvals/actions/{id}/approve — no actor param, no audit_router.append, no transaction around approve+audit); src/butlers/api/routers/approvals.py:2646-2766 (POST /api/approvals/{id}/approve — actor derivation, single transaction wrapping edits+approve+audit_router.append); frontend/src/api/client.ts:3582-3595 (the FE uses only the second)
findings.detail: A second authorization path already exists in the codebase. If a chat confirm is wired to the legacy `/actions/{id}/approve` route — the shape a naive implementer would find first, since it is the one the older `getApprovalActions` client function pairs with — the decision executes with no row in public.audit_log. The chat confirm MUST target the audited route, and the legacy route is a removal candidate now that backward compatibility is waived.

findings.title: Chat-initiated decisions have no attribution slot — they would be indistinguishable from page clicks
findings.evidence: src/butlers/api/routers/approvals.py:1995-2020 (_ACTOR_DASHBOARD = "dashboard:rest-api"; _TELEGRAM_CALLBACK_ACTOR = "owner@telegram"; _decision_actor_id derives provenance solely from X-Butlers-Decision-Actor + callback authentication); src/butlers/api/routers/approvals.py:2721-2729 (audit append uses _decision_audit_actor(actor_id))
findings.detail: The actor vocabulary already distinguishes a Telegram inline-button decision from a dashboard REST decision, and refuses forged Telegram provenance (403/401 at :2003 and :2009). But a confirm pressed inside the chat thread and a click on the /approvals page would both record `dashboard:rest-api`. The audit log would be unable to answer 'where did the owner give consent for this?' — a real gap for a surface whose whole premise is consent-in-conversation.

findings.title: A gated tool called during a chat turn parks an approval the owner's thread never hears about
findings.evidence: src/butlers/modules/approvals/gate.py:900-905 (returns {"status": "pending_approval", "action_id": …} to the model); src/butlers/modules/approvals/park.py:31-104 (writes pending_actions with session_id and fires the owner push); src/butlers/api/routers/conversations.py:798-808 (the SSE stream emits only token + message_complete)
findings.detail: The plumbing for 'butler wanted to act, needs approval' already runs end to end — the action lands in pending_actions with the chat turn's session_id and an owner push is attempted. But the chat thread receives nothing: no SSE event, no card, and (per finding 3) no joinable session_id on the reply row. The owner reads prose about an action whose real state lives on a different page they were never linked to.

findings.title: The dashboard turn ledger already owns at-most-once external effects, but its kind vocabulary excludes actions
findings.evidence: alembic/versions/core/core_193_dashboard_turn_cancellation.py:177-184 (target_kind CHECK IN ('route','bug_report','dead_letter')); :1119-1122 (dashboard_turn_claim_external_action raises 22023 on any other p_kind); :1130-1141 (observes prior Stop and request_id conflict before claiming); src/butlers/core/dashboard_turns.py:286-330
findings.detail: public.dashboard_conversation_turns already implements exactly the semantics a chat-confirmed action needs — claim before the irreversible step, refuse if Stop was requested, expose an 'external_action_in_progress' outcome when a worker crashed mid-effect. An in-thread confirm has no seat at that table, so it would otherwise need a parallel half-happened story rather than aligning with bu-7exe4.14's ledger.

findings.title: Butler pause/resume and trigger cannot be executed by any butler — they are REST-only operator authority
findings.evidence: roster/switchboard/api/router.py:740-862 (POST /registry/{name}/eligibility, writes butler_registry_eligibility_log and log_audit_entry operation="butler_eligibility_set"); frontend/src/api/client.ts:2488-2498 (setButlerEligibility); src/butlers/core_tools/_infra.py:148-183 (trigger() is the only lifecycle-ish core tool, and it spawns rather than administers)
findings.detail: Two of the three action classes the north star names ('pause the finance butler', 'run it now') have no MCP tool surface at all. This is correct and should stay that way — it proves the design must be propose-in-backend / confirm-in-frontend-against-the-page's-own-endpoint, not 'give the butler an admin tool'. Any design that hands butlers registry-mutation tools creates a second authorization path.

findings.title: The frontend already has the exact confirm/undo/honest-receipt primitives, and chat mounts none of them
findings.evidence: frontend/src/hooks/use-approval-decisions.ts:127-145 (approveMut with the honest "Approved. Queued, not yet run. Retry from History." branch keyed on dispatched/status); :180-192 (scheduleDecision over the shared undo window); frontend/src/hooks/use-undo-window.ts:27,72-91; frontend/src/components/butler-detail/ButlerDetailActions.tsx:152-183 (pause behind the same UNDO_WINDOW_MS grace)
findings.detail: The dashboard has already solved in-place confirmation with optimistic drop, rollback, a 5s undo grace, and a receipt that refuses to claim success on a queued-but-undispatched action. All of it is reusable from the chat thread verbatim; nothing new has to be invented for the confirm mechanics.

findings.title: ApprovalDetail is already a complete action-proposal card payload with no chat consumer
findings.evidence: src/butlers/api/models/approval.py:104-160 (title, why, evidence[], blast_radius, reversibility, proposed_action, expires_at, target_contact, referenced_entities, execution_result, push_outcome); src/butlers/core/approvals_hooks.py:53-76 (BLAST_RADIUS_VALUES / REVERSIBILITY_VALUES / DecisionDossier are core-owned and strictly validated)
findings.detail: Everything a good in-thread proposal card must show — what will happen, why, on what evidence, how far the blast radius reaches, whether it can be undone, when the offer expires — is already modelled, validated at the park boundary, and served by GET /api/approvals/{id} (approvals.py:2597). The reversibility enum in particular is the natural gate for whether the card may offer an Undo at all.

findings.title: There is an inventoried, startup-validated exact-argument command registry that no chat surface uses
findings.evidence: src/butlers/modules/approvals/command_contracts.py:27-52 (ExecutableApprovalCommand.materialize rejects any argument-key drift), :63-106 (EXECUTABLE_DIRECT_COMMANDS / NON_MESSENGER_PRODUCER_INVENTORY, including an explicitly non-replayable producer), :126 validate_owner_command_registry; src/butlers/daemon.py:1774-1780 (validated against the live MCP surface before the daemon accepts work)
findings.detail: The repo already has the right shape for 'which commands may an owner-facing surface propose, with exactly which arguments, owned by which butler, and which ones must be refused at queue time'. A chat action registry is an extension of this module, not a new concept — and reusing it means a chat proposal cannot name a command the daemon cannot actually execute.

findings.title: The classifier prompt has no action lane, so action requests are silently coerced into the statement lane
findings.evidence: src/butlers/modules/pipeline.py:560-586 (LANE A data statement/correction, LANE B bug report, plus "If the message is genuinely ambiguous … still call route_to_butler with the best-guess specialist (or `general`)")
findings.detail: 'Pause the finance butler', 'approve that draft email', and 'delete this event' all fall through to Lane A, where the routed butler is told to interpret and apply a statement against its domain schema. For a genuine command this is either a no-op with a confident-sounding reply, or an unrelated write. The ambiguous-fallback clause also routes command uncertainty to `general`, which is the exact silent-routing pattern the 2026-07-28 dossier forbade for questions.

proposals.title: Action proposal cards in-thread, carried on a structured reply wire
proposals.what: Introduce a proposal as a first-class thing a turn can produce, rendered as an interactive card in the thread. Backend: add a sibling core tool `conversation_propose_action(conversation_id, action_id, message)` in a new `src/butlers/core_tools/_conversation_propose.py` (registered alongside `register_conversation_reply_tool`, ToolContext pattern from `_conversation_reply.py:52`). It accepts ONLY an `action_id` that already exists as a `status='pending'` row in the calling butler's `pending_actions` — the butler cannot invent a command, it can only surface one the approval gate already vetted and parked (`src/butlers/modules/approvals/gate.py:900-905`, `park.py:31-104`). Persist it by adding a nullable `proposal_action_id UUID` + `proposal_butler TEXT` column to `public.dashboard_messages` (new alembic core migration; the table is defined alongside `dashboard_conversations`) and threading them through `message_create` (`src/butlers/api/conversations.py:564-612`), `conversation_reply_create` (:700-736), `message_list` (:739-786) and the `Message` API model. Emit a new SSE event `action_proposed` from `_stream_conversation_response` (`src/butlers/api/routers/conversations.py:798`, using the existing `_sse_event` helper at :195), add it to `ConversationSseEventType` (`frontend/src/api/types.ts:5538-5544`) and to the widget's switch (`FloatingChatWidget.tsx:373-439`). Frontend: new `frontend/src/components/chat/ActionProposalCard.tsx`, rendered from `MessageThread.tsx:170` when `message.proposal_action_id` is set. It fetches the dossier via the existing `useApprovalDetail` hook / `getApprovalDetail` (`frontend/src/api/client.ts:3577-3581`) and renders title, why, evidence, blast_radius, reversibility, target_contact and the expiry countdown — the same vocabulary `ApprovalsPage` uses. Confirm / Deny / Later call `useApprovalDecisionMutations()` (`frontend/src/hooks/use-approval-decisions.ts:90-202`) unchanged, so the confirm hits POST /api/approvals/{id}/approve — byte-for-byte the same endpoint, same optimistic cache eviction, same honest 'Approved. Queued, not yet run.' branch as the /approvals page button. Explicitly do NOT add an approve/deny endpoint under /api/butlers/{name}/conversations/**.
proposals.why: This is the whole lens in one move: it turns the thread from a narration surface into a command surface without inventing a second authorization path, because the confirm literally calls the page's own mutation hook. Grounding the proposal in an existing pending_actions row means the butler can never propose something the daemon cannot execute, the dossier (why/evidence/blast_radius/reversibility) comes for free and is already strictly validated in core (`approvals_hooks.py:53-76`), and the owner's consent happens where the context is — in the conversation about the page they are looking at.
integration_points: src/butlers/core_tools/__init__.py (register the new tool on every butler, same always-on rationale as conversation_reply)
alembic/versions/core/ (new migration: dashboard_messages.proposal_action_id UUID, proposal_butler TEXT)

proposals.title: A chat-eligibility taxonomy, with server-side authority extending command_contracts
proposals.what: Codify which action classes may be proposed in chat, gated where, and rendered how. Server authority: extend `src/butlers/modules/approvals/command_contracts.py` with a `ChatEligibility` enum (`gated`, `page_authority`, `never`) attached to each `ExecutableApprovalCommand`, and add a per-tool `chat_eligibility` field to `GatedToolConfig` (`src/butlers/config.py:162, 543-568`) so `roster/{butler}/butler.toml` declares it per gated tool, validated at startup by the existing `validate_owner_command_registry` path (`command_contracts.py:126`, called from `daemon.py:1774-1780`). The taxonomy: (a) GATED — any domain write with blast_radius `contact`/`external` or reversibility `irreversible`; must park through the gate and can only reach chat as a proposal card (rank 1). (b) PAGE-AUTHORITY — operations with no MCP tool and a REST-only operator endpoint: butler pause/resume (`roster/switchboard/api/router.py:740-862`) and force-run/trigger (`ButlerDetailActions.tsx:120-146` → `triggerButler`). These get a distinct lightweight card that calls the *same* client function the page button calls (`setButlerEligibility`, `client.ts:2488-2498`; `triggerButler`), never a butler tool. (c) SELF-SCOPED — approve/deny/defer/retry/abandon of an already-parked approval; direct confirm, since the gate already vetted it. (d) NEVER-CHAT — credential and secret mutation (`src/butlers/api/routers/secrets_v2.py`), approvals policy PUT (`approvals.py:2208`), rule create/revoke (`approvals.py:1424, 1681`), and destructive data ops (`data_ops.py`). For these the butler must render a deep-link card ('open Settings → Secrets') with no control, and the classifier must be told never to propose them. Frontend: `frontend/src/lib/chat-actions.ts` maps a proposal's class to its render component and its dashboard link-back destination — a rendering registry only, never an authorization one.
proposals.why: Without this the proposal card becomes an unbounded remote-execution surface, and an implementing agent has no principled answer to 'can chat rotate a token?'. Anchoring it in `command_contracts.py` reuses a registry that is already validated against the live MCP surface at startup and already knows how to mark a producer non-replayable (`CONNECTOR_ROTATE_TOKEN_PRODUCER`, :83-93) — the exact precedent for a never-chat class. Putting `chat_eligibility` in butler.toml next to `gated_tools` keeps the policy where the risk tier already lives, per-butler and reviewable in git.
integration_points: src/butlers/api/routers/approvals.py:1577-1647 list_gated_tools (surface chat_eligibility so the Autonomy panel shows it)

proposals.title: Propose-then-act: replace the act-first confirm-loop and add an ACTION lane to classification
proposals.what: Two coupled prompt/contract changes. (1) Rewrite the deterministic dashboard block in `src/butlers/core_tools/_switchboard.py:85-108`: split its numbered instructions by intent. For a STATEMENT (a fact the owner is asserting) keep apply-then-confirm. For an ACTION REQUEST (the owner asking for something to happen) the butler MUST route the write through its approval-gated tool so the gate parks it (`gate.py:900-905`), then call `conversation_propose_action` — it must NOT apply first, and must not call `conversation_reply` with a claim that it acted. Make the block state the failure mode explicitly, the way the existing block already does for a missing conversation_reply (:103-107). (2) Add an ACTION lane to the classifier prompt at `src/butlers/modules/pipeline.py:560-586`, alongside the existing statement/bug lanes (and the question lane the north star adds), with concrete examples ('pause the finance butler', 'approve that draft', 'delete this event'). Critically, fix the ambiguity fallback at :576-580: a message that cannot be classified into a lane must NOT be routed to `general` with a best guess — for the action lane it must come back as an in-thread clarifying question naming the candidate actions, preserving the dossier's no-silent-routing-of-uncertainty constraint. Where a butler's write tool is not currently gated but its chat-eligibility class says GATED, that is a butler.toml gap that rank 2's startup validation should surface rather than silently permitting an ungated chat write.
proposals.why: Rank 1 gives proposals a wire and rank 2 gives them a policy, but neither matters while the routed-butler contract still says 'apply it, then ask'. This is the change that makes the owner's Confirm mean something, and it aligns the runtime with the security doctrine it currently contradicts (`about/heart-and-soul/security.md:103-105`: the gate pauses execution and requests confirmation *before* proceeding). The lane fix also closes the specific hole where a command phrased as a request gets interpreted as a domain fact and written somewhere unrelated.
integration_points: src/butlers/modules/pipeline.py:560-586 classifier prompt (ACTION lane + ambiguity fallback)
roster/*/CLAUDE.md Interactive Response Mode sections (propose-don't-apply contract)
