proposals.title: Honest in-thread receipts with a seat in the turn ledger and a link back to the dashboard
proposals.what: After a Confirm, the card must render exactly what happened and where to see it. Four card terminal states driven by the approve response, which is already honest (`approvals.py:2757-2762` sets `dispatched` only when status reached `executed`): EXECUTED (show the effect summary from `execution_result`, plus two links — the canonical `/approvals/{id}` dossier and a class-derived domain deep link from rank 2's registry, e.g. `/butlers/finance` for an eligibility flip); QUEUED-NOT-RUN (say 'approved but not yet run', offer Retry → `retryApproval`, `client.ts:3597-3603`); FAILED (surface the dispatch detail — `_safe_dispatch_detail`, `approvals.py:1033`); AMBIGUOUS. lens:continuity-memory.jarvis_gap: Today the dashboard chat has a thread but no memory and no identity. A thread is a `public.dashboard_conversations` row scoped to one `butler_name`, so the owner's single voice is already forked three ways: the widget's Switchboard threads (`FloatingChatWidget.tsx:99`), the per-butler pinned threads on butler detail pages, and — invisibly — a *shadow duplicate* row that `route.execute` creates on the target butler for every dashboard turn (`_routing.py:1014-1041`), which is where the provider resume handle actually lives. Telegram threads anchor under yet another key, and nothing maps one to the other, so "start on the dashboard, continue on my phone" is not merely unimplemented, it is unrepresentable: there is no owner-level thread object, no conversation URL (`router-config.tsx` has no `/chat` route), and read state lives in one browser's localStorage (`use-chat-unread.ts:38`). Memory within a thread is a 4000-char text preamble of the last five exchange pairs (`conversation_envelope.py:19-59`) — no summary, no pinning, silent amnesia past the truncation — and memory across threads does not exist at all: no MCP tool can read `dashboard_messages`, so a butler physically cannot answer "what did I ask you last week about X", and the only search is an unindexed butler-scoped `ILIKE '%q%'`. Facts learned in chat can reach the graph through the Lane-A route, but they arrive stripped of their origin: the dashboard sender is the bare string `dashboard:operator` that resolves to no entity (`identity.py:221-235` has no dashboard channel), the evidence vocabulary has no `message`/`conversation` kind (`fact_evidence.py:47`), and the reply that reported the write never records which session produced it — `conversation_reply_create` writes `session_id = NULL` every time (`conversations.py:700-736`), so the drill-down link the spec mandates (`dashboard-chat-ui/spec.md:282-291`) is dead code that never renders. The distance to JARVIS is one durable, addressable, owner-scoped thread object with a recall surface over it and honest provenance out of it.

findings.title: Assistant chat replies never persist session_id, so the spec-mandated drill-down link never renders

The spec declares `session_id` as "FK to the butler's sessions.id for assistant responses" and requires the link — this is live spec-vs-code drift. findings.title: Every dashboard turn silently creates a shadow duplicate conversation row on the target butler
findings.evidence: src/butlers/core_tools/_routing.py:902 (source_channel from envelope) and :1014-1041 (conversation_get_or_create_by_thread); src/butlers/core_tools/_switchboard.py:678 (source_thread_identity forwarded); src/butlers/api/conversation_envelope.py:143 (external_thread_id = conversation UUID); src/butlers/api/conversations.py:274-340

Consequences: (1) `conversation_list` (api/conversations.py:137-188) filters only on `butler_name`, so these ghosts appear as empty zero-message threads in the per-butler ChatPanel list; (2) the provider resume handle (`conversation_set_provider_session`, spawner.py:2689-2705) attaches to the ghost, so the thread's real runtime memory hangs off a row the owner can never see or manage; (3) archiving or renaming the visible thread has no effect on where the memory lives.

findings.title: Thread identity is per-butler and per-channel by construction; no owner-level thread object exists

findings.title: No recall surface: no butler tool can read past conversations, and the only search is an unindexed butler-scoped substring match
findings.evidence: src/butlers/core_tools/ (only _conversation_reply.py touches dashboard_messages, and only to write); src/butlers/api/conversations.py:474-505 (ILIKE '%q%'); alembic/versions/core/core_006_dashboard.py:161-165 (only index is conversation_id, created_at)

findings.title: Long-thread memory is a fixed truncation with no summarization, and the classifier lane gets no history at all

findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/chat/FloatingChatWidget.tsx:205-218; src/butlers/api/routers/conversations.py:1596-1603

findings.title: Read state is per-browser localStorage, so no surface knows what the owner has already seen
findings.evidence: frontend/src/hooks/use-chat-unread.ts:38 (WATERMARK_STORAGE_KEY), :50-70 (read/persist), :74-80 (module-scope snapshot)

proposals.title: The owner thread spine: one durable thread across dashboard, Telegram and back
proposals.what: New migration creating `public.conversation_threads` (id UUID7, owner_entity_id UUID NULL, title, summary TEXT, status active|archived, pinned BOOL, last_channel TEXT, last_seen_at TIMESTAMPTZ, created_at, updated_at) and `public.conversation_channel_bindings` (thread_id FK, channel, thread_identity, butler_name, provider_session_id, provider_runtime_type, provider_session_updated_at, UNIQUE (channel, thread_identity, butler_name)); move the core_185 provider-session columns onto the binding and add `dashboard_conversations.thread_id` FK, backfilling one thread per existing conversation and folding shadow anchors (rank 1) into the parent thread. `conversation_get_or_create_by_thread` (`api/conversations.py:274-340`) becomes thread-aware: given `(channel, thread_identity)` it returns the binding's thread. New cross-butler endpoints `GET /api/threads`, `GET /api/threads/{id}/messages` (union of every binding's messages ordered by time, each stamped with its channel), and `POST /api/threads/{id}/handoff` which emits a `notify()` to the owner's Telegram carrying the `/chat/{id}` deep link and pins the Telegram binding to that thread — the "continue on phone" gesture, plus its inverse (a Telegram thread's reply shows in the dashboard widget with a channel chip). Point `FloatingChatWidget.tsx` at `/api/threads` instead of `useConversations(WIDGET_BUTLER)`.
proposals.why: This is the north star for continuity: the thread becomes one durable object the owner moves between surfaces rather than N butler-scoped rows. Everything above (recall scope, read state, summary, provenance) becomes coherent once the thread has an identity independent of butler and channel. It is the highest-cost move here and should follow the cheap repairs, not precede them.

proposals.title: Long-thread management: rolling summary, pin/rename/archive, topic-aware resume
proposals.what: Add `summary TEXT` + `summary_through_message_id UUID` to the thread (or `dashboard_conversations` pre-spine) and maintain it at turn closure: when a thread exceeds the preamble budget, have the Switchboard session write a ≤600-char rolling summary via a new `conversation_summarize` core tool, and change `_build_context_preamble` (`api/conversation_envelope.py:22-59`) to emit `summary + last N pairs` instead of a raw tail — the drop stops being silent. Wire the dead PATCH endpoint: add `updateConversation` to `frontend/src/api/client.ts`, a `useUpdateConversation` mutation, and rename/pin/archive row actions in `ConversationList.tsx` with an `Archived` filter tab (the endpoint and spec already exist). Replace the unconditional resume in `FloatingChatWidget.tsx:205-218`: resume only when the most recent thread was touched within a short window (~30 min) AND its `page_context.route` prefix matches the current route; otherwise open a fresh thread with a one-line "Continue 'Alice's birthday'?" affordance. Also add `"dashboard": "realtime"` to `HISTORY_STRATEGY` (`pipeline.py:92-111`) so the classifier lane sees the thread it is classifying within.
proposals.why: Threads today are immortal, unnameable, unpinnable, and silently amnesiac past five exchanges — and reopening the widget can drop the owner into last week's conversation, pinned to the wrong butler. This turns a growing list of untitled rows into a managed workspace, and it is mostly wiring endpoints and specs that already exist.

proposals.title: Give the dashboard operator a face: resolve the owner entity on every chat turn
proposals.what: Register `"dashboard"` as an identity channel: add a `has-handle`-style mapping (or a dedicated `is-owner-operator` predicate) in `src/butlers/identity.py:221-235` and seed the owner's dashboard handle as an `relationship.entity_facts` triple in a rel migration, so `resolve_and_inject_identity` (`pipeline.py:2778-2792`) returns the owner entity for `dashboard:operator`. Alternatively — cheaper and more honest — short-circuit: when `source.channel == 'dashboard'` and `sender.identity == 'dashboard:operator'`, resolve directly to the owner entity via the existing `public.resolve_owner_triple` SECURITY DEFINER path (`identity.py:844-880`) and set `source_sender_entity_id` on the routed envelope (`_switchboard.py:670-690`). Stamp the resolved entity onto the thread (`owner_entity_id`, rank 6) so recall and facts anchor to a person, not a surface.
proposals.why: The same sentence typed on Telegram and on the dashboard produces different graph anchoring today, because only one of those surfaces resolves the speaker. One owner voice requires one resolved speaker; without it, chat-derived facts have no subject anchor and the butler cannot honestly say "you told me".

proposals.title: Server-side read state so every surface agrees on what the owner has seen
proposals.what: Add `last_seen_at TIMESTAMPTZ` to the thread (rank 6) or `dashboard_conversations`, plus `POST /api/threads/{id}/seen` called when the widget panel is open on a thread and when a Telegram reply is delivered/read. Change `use-chat-unread.ts` to derive the badge from `latest_assistant_reply_at > last_seen_at` returned by the list endpoint, keeping localStorage only as an offline fallback (the `readWatermark`/`persistWatermark` pair at :50-70 stays as the degraded path). Include `unread_count` in the thread list response so the badge needs no client-side diffing.
proposals.why: Read state is currently one browser's localStorage, so a reply read on the phone still badges the dashboard and clearing site data resets the owner's whole sense of what is new. Cross-surface continuity is not just message delivery — it is agreement about attention.
